code: gcd_describe("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort") #> -- Four-Year Cohort Graduation Rate (graduation_rate_4_year_cohort) ------------ #> Share of the four-year high school cohort that graduated, by school, district, #> and state and demographic subgroup, 2004-2025. #>  #> Source: Governor's Office of Education and Workforce Strategy (GOEWS, formerly #> GOSA) #> Years: 2004-2025 #> Detail levels: districts, schools (default), states #> Grain: year, district_code, school_code, demographic #> Key metric: graduation_rate #> Columns: 7, plus 6 joined name columns (see `$columns`); filters: 18 (see #> `$filters`) #>  #> -- Notes ----------------------------------------------------------------------- #> * Missing values: NA means suppressed (small counts), not zero; zeros are real #>   from 2010 on. #> * Limitations: 2004-2010 figures predate Georgia's adoption of the federal #>   four-year adjusted-cohort methodology (ACGR, first reported 2011) and use the #>   state's earlier leaver-based rate; the 2010->2011 state rate drop (~81% to #>   ~67%) is a methodology break, not a real decline <U+2014> do not trend across it. #>   Suppressed cells are NULL (not zero) from 2010 onward, but 2004-2009 sources #>   use literal ZEROS for suppressed cells <U+2014> a zero rate/count in those years may #>   be real or suppressed and cannot be distinguished; treat very small cohorts #>   in 2004-2009 with caution. num_cohort is NULL for every row in 2012-2016 (the #>   source publishes no denominator in those years). The 2004 file lists every #>   public school, including elementary and middle schools with no graduating #>   cohort, so 1,703 of its 2,037 all-students school rows have no graduate count #>   or rate; from 2005 only schools with a graduating cohort are listed (344 in #>   2005). School rows do not always sum to the published district row: of the #>   42,815 district rows (all subgroups) with a published num_graduates and at #>   least one published school value, 468 publish a district num_graduates below #>   the sum of its school rows, 49 of them among the 4,039 all-students rows #>   (source-published, 2005-2025; e.g. 2016 Whitfield 709 vs 810, 2014 Richmond #>   economically_disadvantaged 582 vs 1,286) <U+2014> use the official district/state #>   rows for rollups rather than summing school rows. economically_disadvantaged #>   is not a like-for-like group across years. Statewide it is 55-56% of the #>   cohort in 2017-2021, then 47% (2022), 53% (2023), 61% (2024) and 66% (2025), #>   and district coding shifts: Cobb County puts 98% of its 2021 cohort in the #>   group (36-38% in 2017-2020 and 2023, 20% in 2022) and under 2% of its #>   graduates in 2011, 2012 and 2014, and districts with 100+ graduates that #>   report 10% or less of them in the group or suppress it number 6-11 a year in #>   2021-2023 (0-2 a year in 2016-2020). GOEWS does not document these shifts. #>   The group's graduation rate moves when its membership does, so check its #>   share of the cohort before comparing it across years or districts. The race #>   axis uses the combined asian_pacific_islander bucket <U+2014> not comparable #>   row-for-row with split-convention topics without aggregating those topics' #>   asian + pacific_islander rows at query time.
